newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle sales active at $69 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle sales active at $69 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle Wednesday sold in brisk activity at $69.00 per cwt, up $1.00 from Tuesday and up $3.00 from last week, cattle feeders said.

About 56,200 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, which brought the week-to-date estimate to 106,000, USDA said. Kansas sales were pegged at 20,900, which brought the week-to-date figure to 67,300.

Most of this week's showlists were expected to be sold by the end of Wednesday, although there were reports of a few owners passing bids at $69.00 in hopes of getting $70.00 for their cattle, sources said.
"I sold out this morning, but I honestly think this market will continue going up," one Kansas feedlot manager said.
Gains were attributed to rising beef prices and tight supplies of finished cattle, sources said.
Several loads of cattle that sold Tuesday in Kansas reportedly were being picked up early Wednesday, suggesting packers there were short on inventory, Kansas sources said.

Fed cattle next week were expected to trade at $70.00 amid ideas that showlists will be smaller than this week and contain a greater percentage of unfinished, or "green" cattle, several cattle feeders said.
